provenance.adaptation_note: Parent operator names and workflow are transferred; tactical cards and axis profiles are robotics adaptations, not a claim of upstream robotics clustering.

selection_contract.selection: fit the diagnosed structural gap before considering frequency or venue context
selection_contract.outcome_signal: descriptive audit context only; no acceptance probability
selection_contract.directness_weight: optional venue-routing prior only; no rating or prestige field

main_patterns.name: Audit and Pivot an Assumption
main_patterns.definition: Expose a convention that the field treats as fixed, then replace it with a weaker, testable or structurally different condition.
main_patterns.operational_signature: Name the inherited assumption; show why it is load-bearing; pivot its locus, strength or representation; test the changed condition.
main_patterns.when_to_apply: Use when several recent methods inherit the same unexamined prerequisite and the proposed change can produce a qualitatively new result.
success_conditions: The relaxed condition is exhibited and measurable.
A tightness, counterexample or mechanism test shows the pivot matters.
failure_modes: The result is unchanged after the relaxation.
An equally strong or unverifiable assumption is smuggled back in.

main_patterns.name: Substitute the Operator or Representation
main_patterns.definition: Replace the operator, state representation or computational object that carries the bottleneck while preserving the task contract.
main_patterns.operational_signature: Identify where the old object loses information or creates cost; substitute a new object; isolate the changed object from all other components.
main_patterns.when_to_apply: Use when the task is adequate but the current operator or representation is the binding limitation.
success_conditions: The substituted object is load-bearing and mechanistically justified.
Controls show the gain is not only a larger model or a tuned implementation.
failure_modes: The proposed change is not load-bearing or its evidence cannot separate it from a simpler explanation.

main_patterns.name: Liberate a Fixed Generative Component
main_patterns.definition: Redesign a fixed generator, policy, actuation primitive or synthesis process so it can express the missing behavior.
main_patterns.operational_signature: Find a component whose output space is fixed; change its generation process or factorization; preserve the surrounding evaluation contract.
main_patterns.when_to_apply: Use when a fixed policy, generator or actuation primitive prevents a desired behavior despite adequate supervision or data.
success_conditions: The new process adds a reachable capability rather than another wrapper.
The component-level change is isolated and its new behavior is characterized.
failure_modes: The proposed change is not load-bearing or its evidence cannot separate it from a simpler explanation.

main_patterns.name: Design a Confound-Isolating Diagnostic
main_patterns.plain_language_alias: 设计隔离混杂因素的诊断
main_patterns.definition: Construct a measurement or intervention that separates a claimed mechanism from plausible confounds.
main_patterns.operational_signature: Name one load-bearing variable; perturb it while holding the remaining interface fixed; predict a downstream outcome and include a semantic control.
main_patterns.when_to_apply: Use when a system result can be explained by sensing, compute, data, tuning, human adaptation or another non-mechanistic confound.
success_conditions: The diagnostic changes the downstream outcome, not only a definition of the manipulated variable.
The negative control is matched in cost and preserves the same surface signal.
failure_modes: The proposed change is not load-bearing or its evidence cannot separate it from a simpler explanation.

main_patterns.name: Unify Heterogeneous Inputs into One Space
main_patterns.plain_language_alias: 将异质输入统一到一个空间
main_patterns.definition: Build a shared representation or interface that makes previously incompatible information jointly usable.
main_patterns.operational_signature: Identify the incompatible modalities, embodiments or agents; define a common state or message space; demonstrate the information is used by the decision or control loop.
main_patterns.when_to_apply: Use when the gap is caused by modality, embodiment, sensor or agent fragmentation rather than a missing predictor alone.
success_conditions: The common space preserves task-relevant information across conditions.
Cross-modal or cross-embodiment controls show that alignment is causal.
failure_modes: The proposed change is not load-bearing or its evidence cannot separate it from a simpler explanation.

main_patterns.name: Reframe as a Solvable Object
main_patterns.plain_language_alias: 把不可解问题重构成可解对象
main_patterns.definition: Change the problem object, constraint, state or decomposition so the unresolved question becomes a tractable, falsifiable object.
main_patterns.operational_signature: State the native intractable formulation; define a solvable surrogate with a conservation or approximation argument; test the gap between the two.
main_patterns.when_to_apply: Use when the native robot problem is underconstrained, combinatorial, long-horizon or physically inaccessible in its current form.
success_conditions: The reframe retains the decision-relevant property.
The approximation error or scope boundary is explicit and measured.
failure_modes: The proposed change is not load-bearing or its evidence cannot separate it from a simpler explanation.

main_patterns.name: Manufacture the Supervisory Signal
main_patterns.definition: Create a trustworthy training or adaptation signal from structure, interaction or outcomes when direct labels are unavailable or misaligned.
main_patterns.operational_signature: Locate the missing supervisory information; derive it from demonstrations, contrasts, physics, human feedback or self-consistency; validate that it changes the target behavior.
main_patterns.when_to_apply: Use when data exist but the available label, reward or feedback is too sparse, delayed, unsafe or semantically misaligned.
success_conditions: The signal is tied to the target mechanism rather than a proxy metric alone.
A signal-removal or misplacement control returns performance toward baseline.
failure_modes: The proposed change is not load-bearing or its evidence cannot separate it from a simpler explanation.

main_patterns.name: Encode Structure by Construction
main_patterns.definition: Put geometry, symmetry, contact, safety, timing or interface structure into the mechanism so it is available before optimization or tuning.
main_patterns.operational_signature: Name the invariant or constraint; encode it in morphology, representation, controller, architecture or protocol; test behavior outside the construction examples.
main_patterns.when_to_apply: Use when a structural law is known and repeatedly rediscovered by data, or when deployment requires a guarantee that tuning cannot provide.
success_conditions: The encoded structure is identifiable and survives held-out conditions.
A matched unstructured or post-hoc-regularized control shows why construction matters.
failure_modes: The proposed change is not load-bearing or its evidence cannot separate it from a simpler explanation.

main_patterns.name: Prove Equivalence to Unify
main_patterns.plain_language_alias: 用等价性证明实现统一
main_patterns.definition: Prove that two apparently different objectives, representations or system formulations are equivalent or linked under explicit conditions.
main_patterns.operational_signature: State the two objects; derive the mapping and its assumptions; use the equivalence to remove duplicated machinery or expose a new controllable quantity.
main_patterns.when_to_apply: Use when parallel literatures optimize the same object under different names or when a proof can collapse an apparent trade-off.
success_conditions: The equivalence is exact in the claimed regime.
The practical consequence is more than a renamed formulation.
failure_modes: The proposed change is not load-bearing or its evidence cannot separate it from a simpler explanation.

main_patterns.name: Decompose for Differentiated Treatment
main_patterns.definition: Split a heterogeneous task, population, trajectory or operating regime and treat its parts according to their distinct constraints.
main_patterns.operational_signature: Identify the hidden heterogeneity; partition it by a measurable criterion; allocate distinct mechanisms or policies; test the partition boundary.
main_patterns.when_to_apply: Use when one policy, model or controller is forced to average across regimes with incompatible requirements.
success_conditions: The partition corresponds to a causal or operational distinction.
The per-regime treatment beats a single compromise under matched budget.
failure_modes: The proposed change is not load-bearing or its evidence cannot separate it from a simpler explanation.

main_patterns.name: Decompose and Delegate to Solvers
main_patterns.definition: Break a complex decision into typed subproblems and delegate them to specialized planners, learned modules, agents or tools.
main_patterns.operational_signature: Define the subproblem interfaces; assign each solver a responsibility; verify composition and recovery when a solver fails.
main_patterns.when_to_apply: Use when a long-horizon or multi-agent problem contains reusable subproblems with different algorithmic structure.
success_conditions: Interfaces expose enough state for the delegated solver.
End-to-end gain remains after accounting for coordination and failure recovery.
failure_modes: The proposed change is not load-bearing or its evidence cannot separate it from a simpler explanation.

main_patterns.name: Relax Discrete Search to Continuous
main_patterns.plain_language_alias: 把离散搜索松弛为连续搜索
main_patterns.definition: Replace an intractable discrete search with a continuous surrogate that preserves the decision-relevant objective and can be rounded or recovered.
main_patterns.operational_signature: Specify the discrete object; build a continuous relaxation; characterize the relaxation gap and recovery procedure.
main_patterns.when_to_apply: Use when planning, allocation or design is combinatorial but its geometry admits a meaningful continuous proxy.
success_conditions: The recovered solution respects the original constraints.
The relaxation gives a measurable benefit without hiding an exponential post-process.
failure_modes: The proposed change is not load-bearing or its evidence cannot separate it from a simpler explanation.

main_patterns.name: Adapt by Conditioning, Not Retraining
main_patterns.plain_language_alias: 通过条件化而非重训练实现适应
main_patterns.definition: Adapt behavior through context, system identification or conditioning while keeping the core model or policy fixed.
main_patterns.operational_signature: Expose the changing context; encode it as a condition or online estimate; test adaptation under distribution shift and frozen-core controls.
main_patterns.when_to_apply: Use when online changes are real but full retraining is too slow, unsafe, data hungry or difficult to certify.
success_conditions: The condition captures the shift that matters.
The frozen-core control and recovery test separate adaptation from memorization.
failure_modes: The proposed change is not load-bearing or its evidence cannot separate it from a simpler explanation.

main_patterns.name: Characterize a Limit, Then Surpass It
main_patterns.definition: First establish a boundary imposed by a current formulation, then show a principled mechanism that exceeds or exactly meets it.
main_patterns.operational_signature: State the old limit; prove or measure it under the same regime; introduce one change; show a strict and reproducible improvement.
main_patterns.when_to_apply: Use when a field has a sharp stability, planning, sample, sensing, bandwidth or safety boundary that can be made explicit.
success_conditions: The limit is real under a matched baseline.
The improvement is outside uncertainty and the mechanism explains why the boundary moved.
failure_modes: The proposed change is not load-bearing or its evidence cannot separate it from a simpler explanation.

main_patterns.name: Design a Property-Targeting Pretext Objective
main_patterns.plain_language_alias: 设计针对性质的预训练目标
main_patterns.definition: Construct a pretext or auxiliary objective that targets a property the downstream robot must preserve, rather than generic prediction alone.
main_patterns.operational_signature: Name the downstream property; create a pretext that makes it observable; verify transfer and remove the auxiliary objective as a control.
main_patterns.when_to_apply: Use when the desired property is latent, expensive to label or poorly represented by generic self-supervision.
success_conditions: The pretext predicts the property that matters downstream.
A matched generic pretext does not explain the transfer gain.
failure_modes: The proposed change is not load-bearing or its evidence cannot separate it from a simpler explanation.

subpatterns.name: Relocate the load-bearing locus
subpatterns.tactical_move: Move the enforcement, sensing or control locus to an overlooked state, interface or representation.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when every prior method assumes the same location contains the decisive signal.
success_conditions: The new locus is structurally distinct and observable.
An informed adversary or disturbance cannot erase the signal at the same cost.
failure_modes: The new locus was already used by a close paper.
The move only changes implementation vocabulary.

subpatterns.name: Remove a fixed model assumption
subpatterns.tactical_move: Replace a required model, calibration or distributional assumption with a weaker observable condition.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when the robot must operate under unknown contact, friction, terrain or dynamics.
success_conditions: The weaker condition occurs in the target operating envelope.
A tightness or failure-case analysis shows the removed assumption was binding.
failure_modes: An equally strong hidden model is reintroduced.

subpatterns.name: Replace a distributional condition with a structural one
subpatterns.tactical_move: Move from a fragile statistical prior to a geometric, architectural or interface constraint.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when data coverage is insufficient but physical or system structure is reliable.
success_conditions: The structural condition is independently testable.
The replacement transfers across environments without copying a distribution.
failure_modes: The structural condition is merely a renamed distributional assumption.

subpatterns.name: Characterize the adversarial boundary
subpatterns.tactical_move: Treat a claimed safety, robustness or imperceptibility property as a budget that can be challenged.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when the operating or threat model is stronger than the paper's nominal test.
success_conditions: The strongest relevant disturbance or operator is included.
The boundary yields a reusable design constraint.
failure_modes: Only a static or weak adversary is tested.

subpatterns.name: Pivot the system interface
subpatterns.tactical_move: Move the load-bearing computation across a sensing, communication, human or actuation interface.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when interface latency, bandwidth or authority is the inherited bottleneck.
success_conditions: The interface change is isolated from downstream tuning.
The new interface changes end-to-end behavior.
failure_modes: The interface is changed without a causal account.

subpatterns.name: Isolate a failure-causing convention
subpatterns.tactical_move: Turn a field convention into an intervention and measure the failure it causes.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when benchmark success hides a known deployment failure.
success_conditions: The intervention reproduces the failure and its repair.
The result generalizes beyond one example.
failure_modes: The failure is anecdotal or benchmark-specific.

subpatterns.name: Low-sensitivity operator substitution
subpatterns.tactical_move: Replace an operator whose output is overly sensitive to noise, contact or discretization.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when the same task has a brittle operator-level failure.
success_conditions: Sensitivity is measured at matched compute.
The replacement preserves the task interface.
failure_modes: The gain is only a larger or more heavily tuned model.

subpatterns.name: Curvature-object substitution
subpatterns.tactical_move: Substitute a scalar or local object with curvature, geometry or distributional structure that preserves the missing signal.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when point estimates discard the signal needed for robust state or control.
success_conditions: The extra object has a mechanistic interpretation.
A point-estimate control loses the claimed downstream benefit.
failure_modes: The richer object is used only as an unexamined feature.

subpatterns.name: Representation-level state substitution
subpatterns.tactical_move: Replace the state representation used by estimation, planning or learning.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when the raw state is not invariant to embodiment, viewpoint or contact.
success_conditions: The representation removes a named nuisance without deleting the task signal.
Held-out conditions test invariance.
failure_modes: The representation is an opaque embedding with no failure boundary.

subpatterns.name: Contact and geometry operator substitution
subpatterns.tactical_move: Replace a contact, collision or geometry operation with one that exposes the relevant physical object.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when contact-rich manipulation or non-Euclidean planning is bottlenecked by a standard operator.
success_conditions: The operation is validated on the physical boundary cases.
A geometric or force control explains the improvement.
failure_modes: The operator is a cosmetic reparameterization.

subpatterns.name: Generative process redesign
subpatterns.tactical_move: Change how actions, trajectories or forces are generated instead of adding a downstream correction.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when a fixed policy or generator cannot express the required behavior.
success_conditions: The reachable behavior set expands.
Equal-data and equal-compute controls isolate the generator change.
failure_modes: The generator is only wrapped by off-the-shelf modules.

subpatterns.name: Residual mechanism liberation
subpatterns.tactical_move: Expose the physical or modeling residual that a fixed generator cannot explain.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when sim-to-real, friction, contact or dynamics residuals dominate the error.
success_conditions: The residual is measurable and closed by the mechanism.
A residual-removal control returns performance toward baseline.
failure_modes: The residual model becomes a generic error-corrector with no mechanism.

subpatterns.name: Policy-generation substrate redesign
subpatterns.tactical_move: Change the substrate or factorization from which a policy generates actions.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when policy expressivity or long-horizon composition is limiting deployment.
success_conditions: The factorization matches the action horizon or morphology.
The policy remains stable under perturbation.
failure_modes: Scaling or data alone explains the result.

subpatterns.name: Controlled diagnostic construction
subpatterns.tactical_move: Build a one-variable-isolated intervention or measurement instrument.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when a robot claim can be explained by hardware, data, tuning or human adaptation confounds.
success_conditions: The intervention has a downstream prediction.
Controls are matched in cost and information.
failure_modes: Only the intermediate metric changes, not the task outcome.

subpatterns.name: Cross-modal shared representation
subpatterns.tactical_move: Align vision, touch, language, proprioception or force into a task-usable state.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when modalities are complementary but not jointly actionable.
success_conditions: Each modality has a leave-one-out test.
Alignment improves a downstream decision rather than only retrieval similarity.
failure_modes: The common space is a concatenation with no causal use.

subpatterns.name: Sequential-control re-casting
subpatterns.tactical_move: Recast long-horizon control as a sequence of measurable subgoals or phases.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when a single objective dilutes credit or hides the decisive phase.
success_conditions: The phase boundaries are observable.
The re-casting improves the long-horizon outcome.
failure_modes: The phases are arbitrary labels with no mechanism.

subpatterns.name: Intractable-problem re-casting
subpatterns.tactical_move: Turn a native intractable planning or contact problem into a solvable object with a bounded gap.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when direct optimization is combinatorial, discontinuous or physically inaccessible.
success_conditions: The solvable object preserves the decision-relevant property.
The approximation or recovery error is characterized.
failure_modes: The reframe is a renamed heuristic.

subpatterns.name: Feasibility-object re-casting
subpatterns.tactical_move: Replace an open-ended deployment goal with an explicit operating envelope and feasibility object.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when field performance fails because the target was never bounded.
success_conditions: The envelope is measurable before deployment.
The resulting claim is falsifiable and transferable.
failure_modes: The envelope is selected after seeing the result.

subpatterns.name: Self-supervised signal engineering
subpatterns.tactical_move: Derive supervision from temporal, geometric, cross-view or task consistency.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when robot labels are expensive but structure is observable.
success_conditions: The pretext signal is tied to the downstream property.
Signal removal degrades the intended behavior.
failure_modes: The pretext is generic and unrelated to the task.

subpatterns.name: Residual and latent supervisory signal
subpatterns.tactical_move: Use model residuals, uncertainty or latent disagreement as the training/adaptation signal.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when the error itself identifies where the policy or estimator must change.
success_conditions: The residual predicts the downstream correction.
A shuffled or detached residual is a negative control.
failure_modes: Residual magnitude is optimized as a proxy with no task effect.

subpatterns.name: Human or environment feedback as supervision
subpatterns.tactical_move: Convert intervention, preference, success/failure or contact feedback into a stable learning signal.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when direct reward or labels are absent but the robot already interacts.
success_conditions: Feedback cost and operator burden are measured.
The signal improves behavior without eroding safety or trust.
failure_modes: The system treats feedback as free or ignores operator adaptation.

subpatterns.name: Symmetry-group construction
subpatterns.tactical_move: Encode a symmetry or invariance into the state, model or controller.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when changes of frame, viewpoint, embodiment or ordering should not change the decision.
success_conditions: The symmetry is tested outside training transforms.
Breaking the symmetry produces the predicted failure.
failure_modes: The claimed symmetry is not present in the physical task.

subpatterns.name: Relational topology encoded as structure
subpatterns.tactical_move: Encode contact, graph, topology or relational geometry as a structural prior.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when relations, not individual observations, determine the robot outcome.
success_conditions: The relation is identifiable over standard alternatives.
A topology-free control fails on the same boundary cases.
failure_modes: A topology-as-prior architecture is presented without isolating its work.
subpatterns.upstream_reference: ResearchStudio C13 Relational-Topology Encoded as Structure

subpatterns.name: Embodiment and contact constraint by construction
subpatterns.tactical_move: Build morphology, compliance, contact or actuator constraints directly into the robot mechanism or controller.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when embodiment is the source of the capability, not merely a test platform.
success_conditions: The body–task mechanism is explicit.
A matched embodiment or post-hoc control baseline isolates the construction.
failure_modes: One hardware instance is generalized to all embodiments without evidence.

subpatterns.name: Equivalence-based objective unification
subpatterns.tactical_move: Prove that two control, learning or planning objectives are equivalent in a named regime.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when a duplicated objective or apparent trade-off blocks a simpler design.
success_conditions: The assumptions are explicit.
The equivalence yields a simpler or more powerful robot procedure.
failure_modes: The proof only renames the objective.
subpatterns.upstream_reference: ResearchStudio C06 Probabilistic-Objective Unification via Equivalence Proof

subpatterns.name: Heterogeneous regime decomposition
subpatterns.tactical_move: Split contact, terrain, object, user or agent regimes and allocate distinct treatment.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when a single controller or policy averages incompatible regimes.
success_conditions: The partition variable is measurable online or at design time.
A single-policy control fails under the same budget.
failure_modes: The partition is tuned after results or has no operational meaning.

subpatterns.name: Decompose and delegate to solvers
subpatterns.tactical_move: Give typed subproblems to specialized planners, learned policies, agents or tools.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when planning or coordination contains separable subproblems.
success_conditions: Interfaces and failure recovery are explicit.
Coordination cost is included in the end-to-end evaluation.
failure_modes: A pipeline of modules is called a contribution without a unifying interface.

subpatterns.name: Discrete-search relaxation to continuous
subpatterns.tactical_move: Relax combinatorial planning or allocation into a differentiable or continuous object with recovery.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when a discrete robot decision has exploitable geometry.
success_conditions: Rounded decisions remain feasible.
The relaxation gap is measured.
failure_modes: The post-process secretly solves the original problem at full cost.

subpatterns.name: Adapt by conditioning
subpatterns.tactical_move: Condition a frozen core on the current robot, environment, user or task state.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when the shift is local, recurrent and observable online.
success_conditions: The condition is causally tied to the shift.
Frozen-core, no-adaptation and recovery tests are included.
failure_modes: The method retrains while calling it conditioning.

subpatterns.name: Limit characterization and strict surpass
subpatterns.tactical_move: Establish a stability, safety, bandwidth, sample or planning boundary, then exceed it with a named mechanism.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when a matched baseline has a sharp and reproducible boundary.
success_conditions: The boundary is measured under the same regime.
The improvement exceeds uncertainty and has a mechanism.
failure_modes: Only an empirical improvement is shown with no boundary or tightness.

subpatterns.name: Property-targeting pretext objective
subpatterns.tactical_move: Train on the robot property that must transfer: contact, invariance, uncertainty, affordance or safety.
subpatterns.when_to_apply: Use when generic self-supervision does not represent the property needed downstream.
success_conditions: The pretext targets a measurable task property.
A generic-pretext control and property-removal control are both present.
failure_modes: The property is named after the result or is not observable.

E.strategy_signature_template: Encode the load-bearing body, material and contact constraint into the mechanism, then isolate its contribution against matched embodiment and control alternatives.
E.failure_guard: Do not generalize from one morphology or hardware instance without a mechanism boundary and an explicit transfer test.

P.strategy_signature_template: Design a confound-isolating sensing-to-state diagnostic, and use calibrated or shared representations only when they change a downstream robot decision.
P.failure_guard: Do not report a perception metric gain as a robotics contribution unless the changed state alters task, control or safety outcomes.
P.claim_altitude: state representation, observability or perception-to-action mechanism

C.strategy_signature_template: Audit the inherited model, stability or safety assumption, characterize its boundary, and show a matched mechanism-level improvement under disturbance.
evidence_recipe: semantic negative control on the load-bearing variable
C.failure_guard: Do not call a controller safe or robust from nominal trajectories; identify the boundary and test the intervention on downstream failure.
C.claim_altitude: dynamical mechanism, stability/safety certificate or control law

L.strategy_signature_template: Manufacture a task-relevant supervisory signal or redesign the policy-generation substrate, then prove transfer with signal-removal and held-out embodiment or task tests.
evidence_recipe: held-out task, embodiment or environment transfer
L.failure_guard: Do not present scale, data or a benchmark gain as a learning mechanism without isolating the supervisory signal or policy substrate that caused it.
L.claim_altitude: learning signal, policy-generation mechanism or transfer principle

D.strategy_signature_template: Decompose heterogeneous long-horizon decision structure into typed subproblems, delegate or relax them with explicit interface and recovery guarantees.
D.failure_guard: Do not call a pipeline a planning contribution when the subproblem interfaces, coordination cost or failure recovery are unspecified.
D.claim_altitude: planning decomposition, coordination protocol or long-horizon decision mechanism

H.strategy_signature_template: Construct a confound-isolating interaction or haptic diagnostic whose load-bearing interface changes human–robot behavior, workload, trust or physical safety.
evidence_recipe: delay, novice, expert and failure-boundary tests
H.failure_guard: Do not submit a robot method plus a small user demo to an HRI/HCI venue; the interaction mechanism and human measure must be the contribution.
H.claim_altitude: interaction mechanism, haptic channel or human-factor effect

A.strategy_signature_template: Recast an open deployment goal as a measurable operating envelope, then adapt or diagnose the autonomy loop under real field constraints and recovery failures.
A.failure_guard: Do not equate a single successful run with autonomy; bound the envelope, report recoveries and expose the deployment failure mode.
A.claim_altitude: autonomy loop, operating envelope or deployment mechanism

S.axis_name_zh: 系统集成、实时与基础设施
S.strategy_signature_template: Encode the software–hardware, timing and reproducibility contract into the system architecture, then diagnose end-to-end latency, failure propagation and deployment behavior.
S.failure_guard: Do not present an architecture diagram as a systems contribution without reproducible artifacts and load-bearing end-to-end measurements.
S.claim_altitude: integrated system, real-time contract or reproducible infrastructure
